In humans, this process is important because it ensures that oxygenated blood is efficiently delivered to all parts of the body while deoxygenated blood is returned to the lungs for re-oxygenation. The second circulation, called systemic circulation, involves the left ventricle sending oxygenated blood to the rest of the body via the aorta, and then returning deoxygenated blood to the right atrium. parsed_output.answer: Excretion is the process by which the body removes waste materials and excess substances from the body. In humans, the main organ responsible for excretion is the kidney. The formation of urine involves four main stages: glomerular filtration, tubular reabsorption, tubular secretion, and the formation of concentrated urine. The kidneys filter the blood through the nephrons, which are the structural and functional units of the kidney. Each nephron consists of the Bowman’s capsule, glomerulus, proximal convoluted tubule (PCT), Henle’s loop, distal convoluted tubule (DCT), and collecting tubule. During glomerular filtration, blood is filtered through the glomerulus, and the filtrate moves into the Bowman’s capsule. In the PCT, useful substances like glucose, amino acids, and water are reabsorbed back into the blood. In the DCT and Henle’s loop, further reabsorption and secretion of ions occur. Finally, the remaining fluid, now concentrated, is collected in the collecting tubule and becomes urine, which is excreted through the urinary system.

parsed_output.answer: Mitosis and meiosis are both types of cell division, but they differ in several key aspects. Mitosis is a process where a single cell divides into two identical daughter cells, and it occurs in most body cells. It maintains the same number of chromosomes in the daughter cells as the parent cell. Meiosis, on the other hand, is a specialized type of cell division that occurs only in the formation of gametes (sperm and eggs) during sexual reproduction. It results in four daughter cells, each with half the number of chromosomes of the parent cell. This is why meiosis is also called reduction division. Additionally, meiosis involves two stages (meiosis I and meiosis II), while mitosis involves only one stage. In mitosis, the chromosomes are not paired, whereas in meiosis, homologous chromosomes pair up and exchange genetic material during prophase I. These differences ensure genetic diversity in offspring during sexual reproduction.

For example, tellurium (Te) with an atomic weight of 127.6 was placed before iodine (I) with an atomic weight of 126.9. Another limitation was the placement of dissimilar elements in the same group, such as alkali metals (like Li, Na, K) being grouped with coinage metals (like Cu, Ag, Au), which have different properties. Additionally, the table could not accurately predict the properties of undiscovered elements, although Mendeleev successfully predicted the properties of elements like gallium, germanium, and scandium. The modern periodic table addresses these limitations by arranging elements based on their atomic numbers rather than atomic weights. This change eliminates the problem of anomalous series and ensures that elements with similar properties are grouped together. The modern periodic table also provides a more accurate representation of the electronic configurations of elements, which explains their chemical and physical properties more effectively.

After doing these activities you will notice that the bulb glows only in

· Can you predict the reason for the bulb not glowing in situations 2 and

In class VII, you have learnt that the battery stores chemical energy and
this energy converts into electric energy and makes the bulb to glow as
you observed in situation 1 i.e. the battery supplies the required energy to
make the bulb glow.
But in situation 3, though there is a battery in the
circuit, the bulb does not glow because the connecting wires (nylon wires)
are not able to carry the energy from source (battery) to bulb.
Hence, the nature of the substance plays an important role in the transfer
of energy from battery to bulb.
The material which transfers energy from
battery (source) to the bulb is called a conductor and the material which
cannot transfer energy from battery (source) to the bulb is called a non
conductor.

Drude and Lorentz, at the beginning of the 20 th century, proposed that
conductors like metals contain a large number of free electrons while the
positive ions are fixed in their locations.
Let us understand the behaviour of these free electrons.
Assume that a
conductor is an open circuit.
The free electrons move randomly in the
conductor as shown in fig.- 1.
When the electrons are in random motion,
they can move in any direction.
Hence, if you imagine any cross section
as shown in fig.- 1, the number of electrons, crossing the cross section of
a conductor from left to right in one second is equal to that of electrons
passing the cross section from right to left in one second.
It means that
net charge moving along a conductor through any cross section is zero
when the conductor is in open circuit.
